subject: Post-demo: Nimbus evaluation plan & hallucination probes
messages:
From: michael.grant@redwood.com
To: emma.johansen@stratusai.com, noah.kim@stratusai.com
Cc: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: Nimbus evaluation plan & hallucination probes

Hi Emma/Noah —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for the thoughtful questions — I summarized the key takeaways and proposed next tests below so we can get a direct apples-to-apples comparison between Redwood and the hyperscaler endpoints you evaluated.

Recap (short):
- Primary goals: reduce hallucination rate on knowledge-heavy prompts, maintain sub-150ms median token latency for short chat flows, and get a per-token cost projection for steady-state traffic (~1M tokens/day).
- Current constraints: Stratus needs VPC isolation for any PII, and SOC2 evidence for security review.

Proposed independent evaluation plan (next tests):
1) Quality probes: run the 120 prompt eval (attached eval-probes.csv) across Redwood-hosted M-variants and the hyperscaler cooked model. Track: exact-match, helpfulness, and hallucination tags (binary).
2) Regression sentinel prompts: include 12 high-risk prompts from your production logs (you mentioned the legal Q&A set) as regression checks — failing rate tolerance: <= 5% for hallucinations.
3) Latency & cost micro-bench: 1k warm requests of 1-3 turn conversations; measure p50/p95/p99 token latency and per-token cost on identical instance types.
4) KV-prefix caching test: simulate repeated multi-turn sessions to quantify effective cache hit rate and token savings.

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), eval-probes.csv (prompts + labels).

Asks / next steps:
- Emma: confirm we can ingest the 12 redacted production prompts you mentioned (send via shared Drive link or paste into the Drive folder).
- Stratus: confirm target SLA (latency p95 target) and preferred region.
- Redwood team (cc'd): can you allocate a small evaluation cluster for Thursday (2/19) morning PST to kick off the micro-bench?

I'll put a short canary run results in the Drive and share a quick scoreboard.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform

Thanks Michael — good recap. Quick notes from our side: 

- We can share the 12 redacted prompts today via the Drive folder link you included. Expect them by EOD PST.
- Our p95 latency target for interactive flows is 200ms (we'll prioritize meeting p95 under 300ms), but cost is a hard constraint — we need a projection for 1M tokens/day under both Redwood and the hyperscaler.
- SOC2 evidence: our security team will schedule an intake form next week; they requested sample audit logs for a 7-day window — can Redwood provide a stubbed sample?

One clarification: for the hallucination label, we use a 3-way tag (hallucination/partial/ok). If possible, include both binary and 3-way breakdowns so our reviewers can map to internal severity.

We're fine with your Thursday morning test; can you confirm time (we're PST). Also looping in our infra lead, Noah, to coordinate traffic shaping for the KV-prefix test.

—Emma
Emma Johansen
Head of Product | Stratus AI
emma.johansen@stratusai.com

A couple of risk points: if we can't get the 12 production prompts by Thursday morning, we should still run the public 120-probe set so Stratus sees data. Also, re: cost projection, I'll export the per-instance GPU/hour cost plus infra margin so Emma can map to their 1M-token/day baseline.
